api_key.description: The API key for authentication. Can be set via `PANGOLIN_API_KEY` env var.

ca_cert_pem.description: PEM-encoded CA certificate(s) used to verify the Pangolin server's TLS certificate. Set this when the Pangolin instance is served by a private or self-signed CA. Multiple certificates may be concatenated. Can be set via `PANGOLIN_CA_CERT_PEM` env var.

org_id.description: The organization ID. Can be set via `PANGOLIN_ORG_ID` env var.

tls_insecure.description: Skip TLS certificate verification entirely. Intended for local debugging only — never use against production. Can be set via `PANGOLIN_TLS_INSECURE` env var.

url.description: The base URL of the Pangolin API (e.g. `https://pangolin.example.com`). Can be set via `PANGOLIN_URL` env var.

block.description: Terraform provider for managing Pangolin resources (sites, resources, targets, roles).

name.description: The name of the API key.

secret.description: The API key secret. Only available at creation time; stored in state.

block.description: Manages a Pangolin API key. The secret value is only available at creation time.

actions.description: The set of action IDs to grant. Must be non-empty (the upstream rejects an empty set with a 400 validation error).

api_key_id.description: The ID of the API key whose actions are being managed.

block.description:
Replaces the set of actions (permissions) granted to a Pangolin API key.

The set of valid action IDs is a closed, server-defined enum of camelCase operation names (e.g. `getOrg`, `listSites`, `createResource`). The catalog is not introspectable from the OpenAPI spec; supplying an unknown ID returns a 400 from the upstream API.

> **Note:** the upstream rejects empty sets. To clear all actions, delete the parent API key instead. `terraform destroy` on this resource only removes it from state — the actions remain bound to the key until the key itself is deleted (typically by the parent `pangolin_api_key` resource).

archived.description: Whether the client is archived. Archived clients are kept for audit but cannot connect. Defaults to `false`.

blocked.description: Whether the client is blocked. Blocked clients are denied from connecting until unblocked. Defaults to `false`.

id.description: The numeric ID of the client.

nice_id.description: The human-readable ID of the client.

online.description: Whether the client is currently online.

secret.description: The client secret. Only available at creation time; stored in state.

block.description: Manages a Pangolin OLM (Overlay LAN Manager) client device.

auto_provision.description: Whether to auto-provision users on first login. Defaults to `false`.

email_path.description: The path in the ID token for the user email.

identifier_path.description: The path in the ID token to use as the user identifier (e.g. `sub`).

name.description: The display name of the IDP.

name_path.description: The path in the ID token for the user display name.

redirect_url.description: The OAuth callback URL to configure in your OIDC provider.

tags.description: Optional tags associated with the IDP.

variant.description: OIDC variant. Refines `type = oidc` to a provider family — Pangolin uses this to pre-fill default URLs and tweak the consent flow. One of `oidc` (generic, default), `google`, `azure`.

block.description:
Manages a Pangolin OIDC Identity Provider.

> **Note:** `client_secret` cannot be recovered after import and must be set manually.

org_mapping.description: Expression mapping IDP claims to Pangolin org membership.

role_mapping.description: Expression mapping IDP groups/claims to Pangolin roles.

block.description: Associates a Pangolin IDP with an organization and defines the role/org mapping policy.

expires_at.description: Expiry timestamp as milliseconds since Unix epoch.

id.description: The invitation ID assigned by Pangolin (the first segment of the invite token).

invite_link.description: Full invitation URL including the single-use token. The recipient opens this to accept.

regenerate.description: When `true`, regenerates an existing invitation for the same email instead of erroring on conflict. Defaults to `false`.

role_id.description: Numeric ID of the role to assign once the invitation is accepted.

roles.description: Numeric IDs of the roles attached to this invitation. Mirrors `role_id` today but the API supports multiple in principle.

send_email.description: When `true`, Pangolin sends an invitation email to the address. Defaults to `false` (use the returned `invite_link` directly).

valid_hours.description: How long the invite remains valid, in hours. Server default applies when omitted.

block.description:
Manages a pending invitation for a user to join the configured organization. Invitations are immutable once created — changing any attribute triggers a destroy + create. Use `terraform destroy` (or removing the resource block) to cancel an open invitation.

> **Note:** `invite_link` carries a single-use token in clear and is stored in state. Treat the state as a secret.

billing_org_id.description: ID of the organization that carries the billing account for this org. Usually the org's own ID when `is_billing_org` is true.

created_at.description: ISO 8601 / RFC 3339 timestamp when the organization was created.

is_billing_org.description: Whether this organization carries its own billing account (`true`) or piggybacks on another (`false`).

log_retention_days_access.description: Retention in days for the access audit log. `0` disables retention. Requires an active enterprise subscription on Pangolin Cloud.

log_retention_days_action.description: Retention in days for the action audit log. `0` disables retention. Requires an active enterprise subscription on Pangolin Cloud.

log_retention_days_connection.description: Retention in days for the connection audit log. `0` disables retention. Requires an active enterprise subscription on Pangolin Cloud.

log_retention_days_request.description: Retention in days for the request audit log (proxy traffic). `0` disables retention.

max_session_length_hours.description: Maximum session length in hours before users must re-authenticate. Unset means no enforced cap (server default).

name.description: The display name of the organization.

password_expiry_days.description: Force users to rotate their password after this many days. Unset means no enforced rotation.

require_two_factor.description: Force two-factor authentication for all members of the organization. Unset means inherit the server default.

ssh_ca_private_key.description: Private key of the SSH certificate authority. Returned in clear by the API; stored in Terraform state. Treat the state as a secret accordingly.

ssh_ca_public_key.description: Public key of the SSH certificate authority used to sign user certificates for the Pangolin SSH bastion feature. Distribute to host `TrustedUserCAKeys` config.

subnet.description: The CIDR subnet allocated to the organization (e.g. `100.90.0.0/24`). Set at creation; not modifiable afterwards.

utility_subnet.description: The utility CIDR subnet allocated to the organization (e.g. `100.96.0.0/24`). Set at creation; not modifiable afterwards.

block.description:
Manages a Pangolin organization. Available on self-hosted (OSS / Enterprise) deployments and on Pangolin Cloud. Security policies (`require_two_factor`, `max_session_length_hours`, `password_expiry_days`) and log retention settings are returned by the API as nullable values; leaving them unset lets the server default apply.

> **Note:** `ssh_ca_private_key` is returned in clear by the Pangolin API and stored in Terraform state. Treat the state file as a secret accordingly.

auto_provision.description: Whether to auto-provision users on first login. Defaults to `false`.

email_path.description: The path in the ID token for the user email.

identifier_path.description: The path in the ID token to use as the user identifier (e.g. `sub`).

name.description: The display name of the IDP.

name_path.description: The path in the ID token for the user display name.

org_id.description: The ID of the organization this IDP is bound to.

org_mapping.description: Optional expression mapping a token claim to the org binding. Null when unset.

redirect_url.description: The OAuth callback URL to configure in your OIDC provider. Only returned on create — empty after import.

role_mapping.description: Optional expression mapping a token claim to a Pangolin role for this org. Null when unset.

tags.description: Optional tags associated with the IDP.

variant.description: OIDC variant — refines `type = oidc` to a provider family. One of `oidc` (generic, default), `google`, `azure`.

block.description:
Manages an OIDC Identity Provider scoped to a single Pangolin organization.

This is the single-resource equivalent of combining `pangolin_idp` (system-wide create) + `pangolin_idp_org` (bind to an org): the upstream `/org/{org}/idp/oidc` endpoint auto-binds the new IDP to the calling org at creation time, removing the need for a separate binding resource.

> **Note:** `client_secret` cannot be recovered after import and must be set manually in config to avoid spurious diffs.

apply_rules.description: Enable evaluation of access rules on this resource.

block_access.description: Block all access to the resource.

domain_id.description: The domain ID to attach this resource to.

email_whitelist_enabled.description: Enable the email whitelist on this resource.

full_domain.description: The full domain of the resource (computed).

id.description: The numeric ID of the resource.

nice_id.description: The human-readable ID of the resource.

protocol.description: The protocol (tcp or udp). Defaults to tcp.

sso.description: Enable Pangolin SSO authentication on this resource. Set to false to make the resource publicly accessible.

sticky_session.description: Enable sticky sessions (persistent sessions) on this resource.

subdomain.description: The subdomain for the resource. Set to null to use the base domain.

tls_server_name.description: TLS server name for the backend. Set to null to clear.

block.description: Manages a Pangolin HTTP resource (public reverse proxy endpoint).

expires_at.description: Expiration timestamp (epoch milliseconds). Null when the token does not expire.

id.description: The access token ID (returned by the API).

resource_id.description: The ID of the HTTP resource this token authorizes access to.

session_length.description: Session lifetime in milliseconds, as returned by the API.

token.description: The bearer access token. Only available at creation time; empty after import. Treat as a credential.

token_hash.description: SHA-256 hash of the bearer token, exposed by the list endpoints. Not populated on the freshly-created resource; surfaced on subsequent reads.

valid_for_seconds.description: Lifetime in seconds. When omitted, the API defaults to roughly 30 days (`session_length = 2592000000` ms) and `expires_at` is null (token never expires).

block.description:
Manages a bearer access token bound to a Pangolin HTTP resource.

> **Note:** the `token` (bearer secret) is only returned by the API at creation time. After `terraform import`, the `token` attribute is empty by design — the upstream only exposes a `tokenHash` afterwards. Rotate by destroying and recreating the resource.

Every meaningful attribute is `RequiresReplace`: the Pangolin API does not expose an endpoint to update title / description / lifetime in-place.

extended_compatibility.description: Whether to enable extended compatibility mode. Defaults to `false`.

resource_id.description: The ID of the resource to protect with header authentication.

block.description:
Sets header-based authentication for a Pangolin HTTP resource. Pangolin injects an `Authorization` header into proxied requests. Destroying this resource removes the header authentication.

> **Note:** Credentials cannot be read back from the Pangolin API. After import, you must set `password` and `user` manually to avoid drift detection issues.

password.description: The password required to access the resource.

resource_id.description: The ID of the resource to protect with a password.

block.description:
Sets a password for accessing a Pangolin HTTP resource. Destroying this resource removes the password protection.

> **Note:** The password value cannot be read back from the Pangolin API. After import, you must set the `password` attribute manually to avoid drift detection issues.

pincode.description: The PIN code (numeric string, typically 6 digits) required to access the resource.

resource_id.description: The ID of the resource to protect with a PIN code.

block.description:
Sets a PIN code for accessing a Pangolin HTTP resource. Destroying this resource removes the PIN code protection.

> **Note:** The PIN code value cannot be read back from the Pangolin API. After import, you must set the `pincode` attribute manually to avoid drift detection issues.

resource_id.description: The ID of the HTTP resource.

role_id.description: The ID of the role to assign.

block.description: Assigns a role to a Pangolin HTTP resource.

enabled.description: Whether the rule is enabled. Defaults to `true`.

priority.description: The rule priority (lower number = higher priority).

resource_id.description: The ID of the resource this rule belongs to.

value.description: The value to match against (e.g. CIDR range, IP address, path prefix, country code, ASN).

block.description: Manages an access control rule for a Pangolin HTTP resource. Rules are evaluated in priority order and control which requests are accepted, dropped, or passed through.

resource_id.description: The ID of the HTTP resource.

user_id.description: The ID of the user to assign.

block.description: Assigns a user to a Pangolin HTTP resource.

resource_id.description: The ID of the HTTP resource.

block.description: Adds an email address to the whitelist of a Pangolin HTTP resource.

allow_ssh.description: Whether members of this role may open SSH sessions through the Pangolin bastion.

id.description: The numeric ID of the role.

is_admin.description: Whether this is the built-in admin role of the organization. Admin roles cannot be deleted.

org_name.description: Display name of the organization the role belongs to.

require_device_approval.description: Require an administrator to approve each new device before its user can use this role.

ssh_create_home_dir.description: Whether to create the user's home directory on the host when they first log in.

ssh_sudo_commands.description: List of sudo command patterns allowed when `ssh_sudo_mode = "restricted"`. Ignored otherwise.

ssh_sudo_mode.description: How sudo is gated for SSH sessions opened by members of this role. `none` disables sudo, `full` allows any command, `restricted` allows only `ssh_sudo_commands`.

ssh_unix_groups.description: Unix groups added to the user account on the host when they log in via SSH.

block.description: Manages a Pangolin role. Roles carry both standard RBAC fields (`name`, `description`) and the SSH bastion configuration: whether members of this role may open SSH sessions through Pangolin, how sudo is gated, which Unix groups to grant on the target host, and whether to auto-create a home directory.

user_id.description: The ID of the user to assign.

block.description: Assigns a user to a Pangolin organization role.

address.description: The WireGuard address of the site.

docker_socket_enabled.description: Enable Docker socket access on this site. Defaults to `true` to match the Pangolin API default.

id.description: The numeric ID of the site.

newt_id.description: The Newt client ID assigned to this site. Set at creation time.

newt_secret.description: The Newt client secret assigned to this site. Set at creation time and not retrievable from the API afterwards. Not available after `terraform import`.

nice_id.description: The human-readable ID of the site.

block.description: Manages a Pangolin site (tunnel connector).

alias.description: The internal DNS alias (e.g. `myservice.internal`). Required for `cidr` / `host` modes; ignored / null for `http` mode.

alias_address.description: The resolved alias address, when applicable. Null otherwise.

auth_daemon_mode.description: Auth daemon mode: 'site' or 'remote'. Defaults to 'site'.

auth_daemon_port.description: The auth daemon port (computed by the API).

default_network_id.description: The default network ID, when set by the org configuration. Null when unset.

destination.description: The destination: hostname (`host` mode), CIDR (`cidr` mode), or backend IP / hostname (`http` mode).

destination_port.description: Backend destination port. Required for `mode = http`; ignored for `cidr` / `host`.

disable_icmp.description: Whether to disable ICMP. The server defaults to `false` for `cidr` / `host` modes and `true` for `mode = http`; leaving this unset lets the server pick.

domain_id.description: ID of the parent domain (use the `pangolin_domains` data source to discover). Required for `mode = http`; ignored for `cidr` / `host`.

enabled.description: Whether the resource is enabled. Read-only here; the API returns `true` on creation. Use a future toggle endpoint to disable.

full_domain.description: The full FQDN of the resource. Null otherwise.

id.description: The numeric ID of the site resource.

mode.description:
The mode: `host`, `cidr`, or `http`.

`cidr` / `host` modes are L4 tunnels: the resource requires `alias` and uses `tcp_port_range` / `udp_port_range` for traffic shaping.

`http` mode is an L7 HTTP proxy: the resource requires `domain_id`, `subdomain`, `scheme` (`http` / `https`) and `destination_port`. The server auto-assigns `tcp_port_range = "443,80"`, sets `disable_icmp = true`, and leaves `alias` null.

name.description: The name of the private resource.

network_id.description: The numeric network ID the resource is bound to.

proxy_port.description: The proxy-facing port (server-assigned, read-only). The Pangolin API does NOT accept this as a create input — passing it returns `Validation error: Unrecognized key: "proxyPort"`.

scheme.description: Protocol scheme of the upstream backend. Required for `mode = http`; ignored for `cidr` / `host`. One of `http`, `https`.

site_id.description: The site ID this resource belongs to.

ssl.description: Whether SSL is terminated by the proxy in front of this resource.

subdomain.description: Subdomain to host the proxy at — combined with `domain_id` to produce `full_domain`. Required for `mode = http`; ignored for `cidr` / `host`.

tcp_port_range.description: TCP port range string. `*` for all, `` for none, or specific ports/ranges (e.g. `80,443,8080-8090`). For `mode = http` the server auto-assigns `"443,80"` and ignores any value set here.

udp_port_range.description: UDP port range string. '*' for all, '' for none, or specific ports/ranges.

block.description: Manages a Pangolin private site resource (VPN-accessible endpoint).

client_id.description: The ID of the OLM client to assign.

site_resource_id.description: The ID of the private site resource.

block.description: Assigns an OLM client to a Pangolin private site resource.

role_id.description: The ID of the role to assign.

site_resource_id.description: The ID of the private site resource.

block.description: Assigns a role to a Pangolin private site resource.

site_resource_id.description: The ID of the private site resource.

user_id.description: The ID of the user to assign.

block.description: Assigns a user to a Pangolin private site resource.

enabled.description: Enable or disable this target. Defaults to `true`.

hc_enabled.description: Whether to enable active health-check probing for this target.

hc_follow_redirects.description: Whether the probe follows HTTP redirects.

hc_headers.description: Request headers to set on the probe — list of `{name, value}` objects.

hc_health.description: Current health summary as reported by Pangolin (`unknown`, `healthy`, `unhealthy`).

hc_healthy_threshold.description: Consecutive successful probes required to mark the target healthy.

hc_hostname.description: `Host` header value used by the probe.

hc_interval.description: Probe interval in seconds while the target is healthy.

hc_method.description: HTTP method used by the probe (e.g. `GET`, `HEAD`).

hc_port.description: Port used by the probe. Defaults to the target port when unset.

hc_scheme.description: Scheme used by the probe (`http` or `https`).

hc_status.description: Expected HTTP status code from the probe (e.g. `200`).

hc_tls_server_name.description: TLS SNI used when probing over HTTPS.

hc_unhealthy_interval.description: Probe interval in seconds while the target is unhealthy (typically shorter).

hc_unhealthy_threshold.description: Consecutive failed probes required to mark the target unhealthy.

id.description: The numeric ID of the target.

ip.description: The IP address or hostname of the target (e.g. `localhost`, `10.0.0.1`).

method.description: Scheme used to reach the target (`http` or `https`). Defaults to `http`.

path.description: URL path prefix routed to this target. Combined with `path_match_type`.

priority.description: Routing priority — lower numbers win when multiple targets match.

resource_id.description: The ID of the HTTP resource this target belongs to.

rewrite_path.description: Path the request is rewritten to before being forwarded.

site_id.description: The ID of the site that serves this target.

block.description:
Manages a Pangolin target (backend endpoint for an HTTP resource). Exposes the full health-check (`hc_*`) and request-routing (`path`, `rewrite_path`, `priority`) configuration accepted by the Pangolin API.

> **Note:** `hc_*` fields are sent only when set. Leaving one unset means the server default applies. `hc_headers` is a list of `{name, value}` objects sent as the typed probe header set.

name.description: The display name of the user.

role_id.description: The role ID to assign to the user.

type.description: The user type: 'oidc' or 'internal'. Defaults to 'oidc'.

block.description: Manages a user within a Pangolin organization. Typically used for OIDC-provisioned users.

role_id.description: The numeric ID of the role to bind.

block.description:
Binds an additional role to a user (cumulative). Unlike `pangolin_role_user`, which assigns a single role to a user and strips other bindings, this resource adds one more role on top of any existing bindings. Use it when a user must hold multiple roles simultaneously.

> **Note:** Both attributes are `RequiresReplace` — the binding is identified by its `(user_id, role_id)` pair, so any change creates a new binding and removes the old one.

expires_at.description: Expiration timestamp (epoch ms). Null when the token never expires.

resource_id.description: The HTTP resource this token authorizes.

resource_name.description: Display name of the parent resource.

resource_nice_id.description: Human-readable ID of the parent resource.

site_name.description: Site name for site-level resources. Null otherwise.

title.description: Optional human-readable title. Null when unset.

token_hash.description: SHA-256 hash of the bearer token.

block.description:
Lists every resource access token in the organization.

> **Note:** the bearer secret is never returned by this endpoint — only the SHA-256 `token_hash` is exposed. Filter by `resource_id` in HCL to scope to a single resource.
Retrieves the list of API keys for the organization (secrets are not included).

contents.description: The decoded JSON contents that were applied.

id.description: The numeric blueprint ID to look up.

source.description: Where the apply came from. Observed: `API`, `UI`.

block.description:
Looks up a single blueprint audit record by ID. Returns the same slim fields as `pangolin_blueprints` plus the apply `message` and the raw decoded `contents` (the JSON document that was applied, after base64-decoding).

Use this alongside `pangolin_blueprints` for inspection — e.g. dump the latest blueprint's `contents` to a `local_file` for diff review.

> **Note:** `created_at` is epoch **seconds** (distinct from the ms used elsewhere in the Pangolin API).

source.description: Where the apply came from. Observed: `API`, `UI`.

block.description:
Lists every blueprint audit record for the organization.

Blueprints are an append-only log of past `PUT /org/{org}/blueprint` applies (auto-named with Pangolin's pet-name generator). There is no DELETE endpoint — every record persists. Use this data source for audit reporting or to fetch the latest entry by `id` for inspection via `pangolin_blueprint`.

> **Note:** `created_at` is epoch **seconds** on this endpoint, distinct from the milliseconds used elsewhere in the Pangolin API.

cert_resolver.description: Name of the cert resolver in use, or `null` when the default resolver applies.

config_managed.description: Whether the domain was provisioned via static configuration (`true`) or via the API (`false`).

custom_cert_resolver.description: Custom cert resolver override, or `null` to use the default.

error_message.description: Last error reported during verification, or `null` when no error.

failed.description: Whether the last verification attempt failed.

id.description: The domain ID to look up.

prefer_wildcard_cert.description: Whether to prefer issuing a wildcard certificate for this domain.

tries.description: Number of verification attempts performed by Pangolin.

verified.description: Whether the domain has been verified.

block.description: Looks up a single Pangolin domain by ID. Use this when you already have the `domain_id` and want a one-shot read; for browsing every domain in the org, use `pangolin_domains`.

domain_id.description: ID of the Pangolin domain whose DNS records to retrieve.

base_domain.description: Name the record applies to (may be a wildcard, e.g. `*.example.com`).

domain_id.description: ID of the domain this record belongs to.

id.description: Numeric ID of the DNS record.

value.description: Record value (IP, target name, TXT content, etc.).

verified.description: Whether Pangolin has verified that the record is published on the authoritative nameserver.

records.description: The DNS records associated with the domain.

block.description: Lists the DNS records Pangolin expects (or has verified) for a domain — useful to feed an external DNS-as-code provider that publishes them on your authoritative nameserver.

cert_resolver.description: Name of the cert resolver in use, or `null` when the default resolver applies.

config_managed.description: Whether the domain was provisioned via static configuration (`true`) or via the API (`false`).

custom_cert_resolver.description: Custom cert resolver override, or `null` to use the default.

error_message.description: Last error reported during verification, or `null` when no error.

failed.description: Whether the last verification attempt failed.

prefer_wildcard_cert.description: Whether to prefer issuing a wildcard certificate for this domain.

tries.description: Number of verification attempts performed by Pangolin.

verified.description: Whether the domain has been verified.

block.description: Retrieves the list of domains for the organization.

auto_provision.description: Whether users are auto-provisioned on first login.

variant.description: OIDC variant refinement — one of `oidc` (generic), `google`, `azure`. Useful to branch on provider family without parsing the name.

block.description: Retrieves the list of Identity Providers configured in the system.

count.description: Number of requests originating from this country.

requests_per_country.description: Request count broken down by ISO-3166 country code resolved from the client IP.

requests_per_day.description: Request count broken down by day, with allowed / blocked / total triplets.

resource_id.description: Narrow the analytics to a single resource (numeric ID, encoded as string for the API).

time_end.description: End of the time range as an ISO 8601 / RFC 3339 timestamp. Defaults to the current time when omitted.

time_start.description: Start of the time range as an ISO 8601 / RFC 3339 timestamp. Defaults to 7 days ago when omitted.

total_blocked.description: Total number of blocked (denied) requests over the queried range.

total_requests.description: Total number of requests over the queried range (allowed + blocked).

block.description:
Returns the request analytics rollup of the configured organization — same view the Pangolin web UI displays under "Logs > Analytics". Three breakdowns: by country, by day, and global totals.

> **Note:** Requires an active enterprise subscription on Pangolin Cloud. Always available on self-hosted enterprise installs.

billing_org_id.description: The billing org reference. Null in self-host.

created_at.description: ISO-8601 timestamp of when the organization was created.

is_billing_org.description: Whether this org carries the billing account. Null in self-host.

max_session_length_hours.description: Maximum session length in hours. Null when inheriting.

password_expiry_days.description: Password expiry policy in days. Null when inheriting.

require_two_factor.description: Whether 2FA is required for users. Null when the org inherits the default.

settings_log_retention_days_access.description: Access audit log retention in days. 0 means disabled.

settings_log_retention_days_action.description: Action audit log retention in days. 0 means disabled.

settings_log_retention_days_connection.description: Connection audit log retention in days. 0 means disabled.

settings_log_retention_days_request.description: Request audit log retention in days. 0 means disabled.

ssh_ca_private_key.description: The org's SSH CA private key. Treat as a credential.

ssh_ca_public_key.description: The org's SSH CA public key.

block.description:
Lists every organization visible to the calling API key. Useful for multi-org admin workflows and audit reporting.

> **Note:** root-only — fails with HTTP 403 when the provider's API key is not server-admin scoped. The `ssh_ca_private_key` attribute carries the org's SSH CA private key in clear; treat it as a credential.

reason.description: Numeric reason code for the access decision.

resource_id.description: Numeric ID of the resource that received the request.

resource_name.description: Display name of the Pangolin resource that received the request.

resource_nice_id.description: Human-readable nice ID of the Pangolin resource.

site_resource_id.description: Numeric ID of the site-scoped resource that handled the request, if any.

timestamp.description: Unix epoch seconds when the request was processed.

tls.description: `true` when the request was received over TLS.

user_agent.description: `User-Agent` header of the request. Null when not sent.

resources.description: Distinct resources seen, as `{id, name}` pairs.

filter_attributes.description: Distinct values observed in the result set for each filterable dimension. Useful to populate UIs with allowed values to refine the query.

host.description: Filter by the `Host` header of the request.

limit.description: Maximum number of entries to return. The API enforces its own ceiling.

location.description: Filter by client geolocation string as resolved by Pangolin.

method.description: Filter by HTTP method. One of `GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `DELETE`, `PATCH`.

offset.description: Skip the first N entries in the result set. Use with `limit` to paginate.

path.description: Filter by URL path of the request.

reason.description: Filter by the access decision reason code emitted by Pangolin.

resource_id.description: Filter by the numeric ID of the resource that received the request.

time_end.description: End of the time range as an ISO 8601 / RFC 3339 timestamp. Defaults to the current time when omitted.

time_start.description: Start of the time range as an ISO 8601 / RFC 3339 timestamp (e.g. `2026-05-01T00:00:00Z`). Defaults to 7 days ago when omitted.

total.description: Total number of entries matching the filter, ignoring pagination.

block.description:
Queries the request audit log of the configured organization. This is the same log the Pangolin web UI displays under "Logs > Requests". All filter attributes are optional; the API defaults to the last 7 days when `time_start` is omitted.

> **Note:** Field types match what the Pangolin API actually returns. `timestamp`, `reason`, `resource_id` and the IDs are integers; `action` is a boolean (`true` = request was allowed, `false` = denied). `metadata`, `headers` and `query` come back as JSON strings; use `jsondecode()` to access their fields. `raw_json` on each entry preserves the full server payload as a fallback.

resource_id.description: Numeric ID of the HTTP resource whose roles to list.

is_admin.description: Whether the role is the built-in admin role of its organization.

roles.description: Roles granted access to the resource.

block.description: Lists the roles currently granted access to a Pangolin HTTP resource. The full role definition (SSH bastion settings, etc.) is available on `pangolin_roles`; this data source returns the slim summary the resource-scoped endpoint emits.

resource_id.description: Numeric ID of the HTTP resource whose targets to list.

enabled.description: Whether the target is currently enabled.

hc_enabled.description: Whether the active health check is enabled.

hc_follow_redirects.description: Whether the probe follows HTTP redirects.

hc_headers.description: Probe request headers — list of `{name, value}` objects.

hc_healthy_threshold.description: Consecutive successful probes required to mark the target healthy.

hc_hostname.description: Hostname used by the health-check probe.

hc_interval.description: Probe interval in seconds when the target is healthy.

hc_port.description: Port used by the health-check probe.

hc_status.description: Expected HTTP status code from the probe (e.g. `200`).

hc_tls_server_name.description: TLS SNI used when probing over HTTPS.

hc_unhealthy_interval.description: Probe interval in seconds when the target is unhealthy.

hc_unhealthy_threshold.description: Consecutive failed probes required to mark the target unhealthy.

method.description: Scheme used to reach the target (`http` or `https`).

path.description: URL path prefix this target serves.

resource_id.description: ID of the resource this target belongs to.

rewrite_path.description: Path the request is rewritten to before being forwarded.

site_id.description: ID of the site that serves this target.

block.description:
Lists the backend targets of a Pangolin HTTP resource, with the full list-view detail (site labels, health-check configuration, path routing) that the per-id `GET /target/{id}` endpoint does not echo.

> **Note:** Health-check fields (`hc_*`) and routing fields (`path`, `rewrite_*`, etc.) come back as `null` when no probe / no routing is configured — surfaced as Terraform `null` in those cases.

docker_socket_enabled.description: Whether Docker socket access is enabled on the site.

endpoint.description: Current public WireGuard endpoint (`ip:port`) of the connector.

exit_node_id.description: ID of the exit node this site is bound to (null when none).

last_bandwidth_update.description: ISO 8601 / RFC 3339 timestamp of the last bandwidth counter update.

last_hole_punch.description: Unix epoch seconds of the last successful NAT hole punch.

last_ping.description: Unix epoch seconds of the last successful keep-alive from the connector.

listen_port.description: Listen port currently used by the connector behind NAT.

megabytes_in.description: Total bytes received by the site, expressed in MB.

megabytes_out.description: Total bytes sent by the site, expressed in MB.

newt_id.description: Newt connector identifier assigned to the site.

nice_id.description: Nice ID of the site to look up (e.g. `smart-marbled-salamander`).

online.description: Whether the site is currently online.

pub_key.description: WireGuard public key of the site connector (newt).

public_key.description: WireGuard public key of the central exit / hub side of the tunnel.

subnet.description: WireGuard subnet allocated to the site.

block.description: Looks up a single Pangolin site by its nice ID (the human-readable identifier shown in the Pangolin UI). Returns the full site payload — traffic counters, WireGuard public keys, last ping, status, etc. — that the list endpoint does not expose.

alias_address.description: The resolved alias address. Null when unset.

default_network_id.description: The default network ID. Null when unset.

destination_port.description: The destination port. HTTP-mode resources only; null otherwise.

domain_id.description: The associated domain ID. Null when unset.

full_domain.description: The full FQDN of the resource. Null when unset.

proxy_port.description: The proxy-facing port. HTTP-mode resources only; null otherwise.

scheme.description: The protocol scheme. HTTP-mode resources only; null otherwise.

site_id.description: The parent site ID (first entry of the upstream `siteIds` array).

ssl.description: Whether SSL is terminated by the proxy.

subdomain.description: The configured subdomain. Null when unset.

email.description: Email address claimed by the IDP. Null when none was provided.

idp_id.description: Numeric ID of the IDP that issued this username. Use `pangolin_idps` to discover available IDPs.

is_owner.description: Whether the user owns the organization.

name.description: Display name claimed by the IDP. Null when none was provided.

roles.description: Roles currently assigned to the user, as `{role_id, role_name}` pairs.

two_factor_enabled.description: Whether two-factor authentication is enabled for this user.

username.description: Username to look up (the value Pangolin received from the IDP).

block.description:
Looks up a Pangolin user by their `username` within an IDP. Usernames are unique only within an IDP, so the `idp_id` input is required — matching the underlying `GET /org/{org}/user-by-username` contract.

> **Note:** This data source returns `null` for `email` and `name` when the user has not yet logged in or did not share these claims with Pangolin. Treat them as eventually-consistent.

date_created.description: ISO-8601 timestamp of when the user was created.

email_verified.description: Whether the user's email address has been verified.

idp_id.description: The numeric ID of the IDP that provisioned this user. Null for internal users.

idp_name.description: The display name of the IDP that provisioned this user. Null for internal users.

name.description: The user's display name. Null when unset.

server_admin.description: Whether the user holds server-admin (root) scope.

two_factor_enabled.description: Whether the user has 2FA enrolled and active.

two_factor_setup_requested.description: Whether the user has been asked to set up 2FA on next login.

type.description: Account type — `internal` for local accounts, otherwise the IDP variant name.

user_id.description: The user ID to look up.

block.description:
Looks up a Pangolin user by their cross-org `user_id`.

Distinct from `pangolin_user` (keyed by `username + idp_id` within an org). This data source queries the root-only `GET /user/{userId}` endpoint and surfaces extra fields not exposed by the org-scoped variant: `server_admin`, `two_factor_setup_requested`, `email_verified`, `date_created`, `idp_name`.

> **Note:** root-only — fails with HTTP 403 when the provider's API key is not server-admin scoped.

agent.description: Filter by device agent. One of `windows`, `android`, `cli`, `olm`, `macos`, `ios`, `ipados`, `unknown`.
Device agent. One of `windows`, `android`, `cli`, `olm`, `macos`, `ios`, `ipados`, `unknown`. Null when unknown.

approval_state.description: Approval state when device approval is enabled. Null otherwise.

megabytes_in.description: Cumulative inbound traffic in MB. Null when the counters haven't been populated yet.

megabytes_out.description: Cumulative outbound traffic in MB. Null when the counters haven't been populated yet.

olm_archived.description: Whether the underlying OLM tunnel is archived.

olm_version.description: OLM agent version when applicable. Null otherwise.

online.description: Whether the device is currently online.

org_name.description: Display name of the parent organization.

pub_key.description: Wireguard public key. Null when the device hasn't completed handshake.

type.description: Connection type — `olm` for org-level connectors, otherwise an end-user device type.

user_email.description: Email of the bound user. Null for org-level devices.

user_id.description: ID of the user this device is bound to. Null for org-level devices.

username.description: Username of the bound user. Null for org-level devices.

status.description: Filter by device approval / lifecycle status. Each entry is one of `active`, `pending`, `denied`, `blocked`, `archived`. Default: `["active", "pending"]`.

total.description: Total number of devices matching the filters (across all pages).

block.description:
Lists the user-bound devices for an organization — phones, laptops, browsers, anything with a per-user binding. Distinct from `pangolin_clients` (org-level OLM clients with no user association).

All filter attributes are optional; when omitted, the upstream applies its defaults (`page_size = 20`, `status = ["active", "pending"]`, `order = "asc"`).

> **Note:** the item shape is inferred from the sibling `GET /org/{org}/clients` endpoint (same `Client` OpenAPI tag, same "Clients retrieved successfully" message). The `sites` field is intentionally omitted until a real value is observed — its element shape can't be guessed safely from spec alone.
